Bernard Circas was a Sordish poet, novelist, short story writer and communist politician. He was acclaimed for his lyrical flow and was regarded to be the leader of the Sordish avant-garde. He was killed by a member of the Young Sords during Anton Rayne’s inauguration ball.

His early writings were heavily influenced by the social, cultural, and economic problems of his home city of Deyr. His work earned him the description of a ‘romantic communist.’

He joined the Red Youth during the Sordish Civil War, and fled Sordland after the war was over, surviving the purge of Tarquin Soll. He moved to United Contana and studied sociology at the Communist University of Kyow. There, he was influenced by the artistic experiments of Contanan poets who advocated futurism, as well as the ideological vision of Malenyev.

His literary works are widely regarded as seminal contributions to Sordish literature and have garnered numerous international accolades. He was the second individual from Sordland to receive the prestigious Vulpitzer Award in 1948, following Herman Equa. Due to his political views, however, his works have been subject to a ban in Sordland since 1930.

In 1950, Bernard returned to Sordland following the departure of Tarquin Soll. He organized strikes against Sordish government’s failure to include amnesty laws and started to become a popular figure in Sordish politics. He ran as an independent in the 1953 General Elections and became the first communist to be elected to the Grand National Assembly of Sordland.

He was shot when he was leaving Anton Rayne’s inauguration ball by a member of the Young Sords.

Konrath Koronti was the CEO and majority shareholder of the HOS Conglomerate. He is the man who created the famous Koronti brand through his highly successful business ventures and motivational quotes that inspired generations of entrepreneurs. He always promoted a victory no matter the cost approach to making a business a success which also drew criticism from those who parted ways with him on his ventures.

The rise of the Heart of Sordland Conglomerate is entirely on the shoulders of Konrath Koronti who acquired small companies in critical industries where Sordland was lagging behind. His competition and performance oriented attitude allowed him to disrupt these industries and to dominate them.

He had five children whom he is said to have raised without excessive wealth and privilege. Konrath Koronti passed away at the Emerald Hospital in Holsord on January 20th, 1954 due to cirrhosis.

Marcel Koronti is a Sordish businessman, philanthropist, entrepreneur who is the son of the famous media proprietor Konrath Koronti. He is the chairman of HOS conglomerate, Sordland’s largest conglomerate operating in the media, energy, construction, trade and tourism industries. He is also the chairman of Sordland Today, the most influential newspaper of Sordland, and operates HOS Advertising, the largest advertising company of Sordland. He previously served as the chairman of HOS Resorts, a luxury hotel group with 12 destinations in 8 countries.

Koronti obtained a bachelor's degree from the Perla School of Business and a master's degree in media and communications from Harcard University in Ventrie City, Arcasia.

In 1940, Koronti joined the Sordish Broadcasting Corporation as vice president in charge of advertising, before being transferred to the HOS Resorts chain by Konrath Koronti three years later. He transformed HOS Resorts from a leading hotel chain in Sordland into an international powerhouse through his expansion of the brand into 7 different countries.

In 1950, he left HOS Resorts and started operating the HOS Advertising, the advertising company within the HOS Media Group of the HOS conglomerate.

After his father’s death in 1954, he was elected as the next chairman of HOS. His wealth is estimated to be around a couple billion SR. According to the Ekonomists, he is one of the three richest Sords alive today.

Evelyn Vectern is a Sordish journalist, author and school teacher who is the wife of Petr Vectern, the current Vice President of Sordland. In 1953, to help support her husband in his political career, she ended her career as a teacher of literature at the prestigious Holsord State High School.

After graduating from the Holsord State University, Vectern started working as an editor in the magazine, Kosmopolit. She married Petr Vectern in 1936.

Vectern later joined the Holsord Post as a journalist where she became known for her pro-government articles throughout the late 1940’s. Simultaneously, she started working as a teacher of literature at the Holsord State High school.

She was expelled from the newspaper after defending Ewald Alphonso and writing about a ‘conspiracy by the state apparatus’. In 1953, she quit her job to support Petr Vectern’s candidacy as the running mate of Anton Rayne.

Ilana Vance was a Rumburgian spy who briefly served as the private secretary of President Anton Rayne under the alias “Livia Suno.” During her service in Sordland, she was tasked with directly handling most of the critical calls, scheduling and paperwork for the president.

Vance had previously worked at the Sordish Airlines headquarters as the secretary of the director, before starting her work for the United Sordland Party National Committee in 1953, where she was assigned to assist Petr Vectern, who was organizing support for presidential nominee Anton Rayne.

After Rayne’s successful election, Vance began serving as the personal secretary in Rayne’s office at the Maroon Palace. She served as President Rayne’s secretary until 1956 when she was arrested after her identity was uncovered by a state investigation. She is being held in Antel Rock Prison.

Livia Suno is the former private secretary of President Anton Rayne. She was tasked with directly handling most of the critical calls, scheduling and paperwork for the president. She was dismissed from her position in 1956.

Suno had previously worked at the Sordish Airlines headquarters as the secretary of the director, before starting her work for the United Sordland Party National Committee in 1953, where she was assigned to assist Petr Vectern, who was organizing support for presidential nominee Anton Rayne.

After Rayne’s successful election, Suno began serving as the personal secretary in Rayne’s office at the Maroon Palace. She served as President Rayne’s secretary until 1956.

Serge Wolkner is a Sordish driver who serves as the presidential driver of President Anton Rayne.

Born in the small town of Nehir, between Erzaren and Deyr, Wolkner attended the Deyr Dastnurity School. He then attended Holsord State University. After his graduation, he had to leave the capital due to lack of jobs at the time, and briefly worked as a truck driver between the cities of Anrica and Lachaven. He later entered the Sordish Police Academy, but despite completing his training, he did not join the police forces. He briefly worked as a private bodyguard in Holsord before entering the special training course of the Maroon Palace.

After completing his extensive training of protective driving, firearms and first-aid, he joined the service of the Maroon Palace as a driver in 1930. He was tasked with driving various guests of the state, as well as transporting certain documents and goods to the Maroon Palace.

He was chosen to be the presidential driver in 1954 after the departure of Nouman Fevon who was the driver of both President Soll and Alphonso. Serge is the most experienced driver in the service of the Maroon Palace, having served for over twenty years.

After completing his extensive training of protective driving, firearms and first-aid, he joined the service of the Maroon Palace as a driver in 1930. He was tasked with driving various guests of the state, as well as transporting certain documents and goods to the Maroon Palace.

He was chosen to be the presidential driver in 1954 after the departure of Nouman Fevon who was the driver of both President Soll and Alphonso. Serge was the most experienced driver in the service of the Maroon Palace, having served for over twenty years.

During a military parade in 1957, he was killed by assassins who attempted to kill President Rayne. Today, he is regarded as a national hero who saved Anton Rayne by taking the bullet.
